newsitem.title: USA: Agouron reports postitive Viracept results.
newsitem.headline: Agouron reports postitive Viracept results.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc said Thursday that its Viracept AIDS drug candidate produced a significant reduction in viral load and improvement in T cell counts in three separate clinical trials.
Viracept is a protease inhibitor currently before the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for approval.

In the first study, patients were treated with Viracept alone; in the second they were given Viracept along with the drug d4T; and in the third trial they were given Viracept in combination with AZT and 3TC.

The treatments containing Viracept were compared with control arms containing the other drug combinations, without Viracept. Agouron said the trials containing Viracept produced significantly higher improvements in viral load and T cell count, when compared with the control arms.

It also said Viracept was safe and well tolerated, and did not produce some of the side effects observed with other protease inhibitors. However, it said some moderate and more frequent diarrhea was reported.
Agouron said that of the 696 patients treated with Viracept in the trials, only one possible significant drug reaction was reported.
Agouron also said that preliminary data indicates that Viracept combined with another protease inhibitor, Hoffman-La Roche's saquinavir, "may be a useful therapy."
After 12 weeks of treatment with the two drugs, the median decrease in viral load of 13 patients was 99 percent, and the median T cell increase was 118 cells.
It said that drug combination was generally well tolerated and that an expanded trial is in progress.
In addition, a Phase I pediatric study in children aged two to 13 years showed Viracept oral powder and tablets were safe and well tolerated.
